story.title: Kintsugi - The Japanese Art of Mending
paragraphs_en: Craaash...!! "Tina, what have you done? It was a very costly pot!"
"Ameena, how was your day at school?" Abba asked. "Not so good, Abba. My best friend Tina was upset. She broke a very costly pot in her father's shop by mistake. " "Oh! Can't it be mended?"
"How can anyone mend a broken pot, Abba?" Ameena was curious. "Well, it is an art my child. An ancient art." said Abba. "Ancient art!" exclaimed Ameena. "Please,tell me more about it, Abba."

"Kintsugi is an ancient Japanese art of mending broken pottery. Folktales say it originated in the 15th century after a Japanese king sent a tea bowl for repair to China but the result was ugly." Abba narrated the story. "So did he throw away the bowl?" asked Ameena.

"No my child. The Japanese artisans worked on it and found a unique way to mend the pot." "Really, how Abba?" "They used lacquer mixed with gold powder. Not only was the pot repaired it looked beautiful too." replied Abba.
"This Japanese art is mostly used on ceramic ware. The philosophy is to encourage mending and now artisans use different techniques and colours to do the same."

"Thank You Abba!" said Ameena. "Tomorrow, I will tell Tina about Kintsugi. I am sure she will be happy to know that broken pots can be repaired." "Oh, but don't go around breaking pots to repair them later." said Abba with a hearty laugh.
